time.desc: For the first time, one government publicly stated "regime change of the other party" as a foreign policy goal and accompanied it with a tough warning on nuclear issues. The other party's senior officials immediately responded hard and stated that they would only negotiate based on mutual respect.

The two sides initiated indirect negotiations at the technical level through a third-party intermediary. At the same time, the other party held live-fire drills near key sea lanes and briefly announced that the lane was restricted.
The mediator publicly stated that an agreement between the two parties was "close at hand", sending a signal that a consensus was close to being reached.

The two countries and their allies launched large-scale joint air strikes against each other. The conflict escalated from a diplomatic confrontation to an open war, and there was confirmation that the highest-level officials were killed.

For the first time, one of the participating parties publicly admitted that the death of its own soldiers during the operation was due to the other party's drone counterattack on its overseas support facilities.

The warring parties officially confirmed that the wartime supreme leader has completed the succession and handover and mobilized internally to consolidate power, showing that the regime has not collapsed due to "decapitation strikes"

Senior officials from one of the parties involved in the war made a clear statement on the navigation policy of key sea lanes, stating that they had no objection to the passage of ships from some third countries and linked their energy policy to the duration of the war.

The leaders of one of the parties involved in the war issued a time-limited ultimatum on the reconstruction of the channel, threatening to attack the other side's power and other civilian infrastructure to force the resumption of shipping.
The other party's armed forces publicly warned that if its energy facilities were attacked, they would completely close key sea lanes, escalating the threat of "blockade"

One party participating in the war announced that it has opened dialogue with the other party and promised to temporarily suspend attacks on the other party's energy facilities to provide a window period for negotiations.
One party participating in the war formally submitted an armistice plan containing multiple clauses to the other party to promote the end of the conflict and deal with the channel crisis.

The other party gave a formal response to the multi-term armistice plan, which brought the negotiation to a new stage. At the same time, the military command personnel related to the channel blockade were targeted and killed, and it was publicly reported.
Major countries outside the region jointly proposed an alternative five-point plan to end the war, calling for an immediate ceasefire and the restoration of normal traffic on key sea lanes.

The leader of one side of the war gave a nationally televised address, announcing that he would impose harsher attacks on the other side in the coming weeks and reiterated his hope of ending the conflict in the short term.

The leader of one side of the war once again publicly threatened to bomb the other side's power, transportation and other civilian infrastructure and demanded that the channel be reopened. The other camp then threatened to expand the blockade of another key shipping chokepoint.

One country deployed an anti-drone laser system in a city in another country and temporarily closed the airspace over the city, causing the cancellation of multiple inbound and outbound flights at the airport.
The leader of a country publicly accused his opponent of violating the existing ceasefire arrangement and warned of consequences, which was in contrast to his optimistic statement a few hours ago.

One country's mainstream media revealed that its government is discussing plans to carry out military strikes against its opponents' nuclear facilities and is evaluating options to expand attacks by the end of the year.
The rival military launched a new missile offensive and fired missiles at an opponent's warship, while denying that it had closed the key strait.

For the first time, security figures from allies of the party launching the air strikes admitted that its air strikes had no feasible plan for regime change and that relying on bombing to trigger a popular uprising was wishful thinking.

The warring parties carried out air strikes on the air defense and naval facilities of the opponent's largest crude oil export hub. Multiple explosions were heard on the island, and energy supply risks spilled over.
